page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The planar BO₃ unit
lines: Draw one boron atom with three OH groups
Boron is sp² hybridised, so the three
O–B–O angles are 120° and the BO₃ unit
steps.why: The drawing has to show three OH groups on one boron at 120°, because those two features are what make it a boric acid molecule rather than any other three-armed unit.
common_mistakes: Drawing the three hydrogen atoms bonded to boron. They sit on the oxygen atoms, as OH groups.
Drawing a pyramid. Boron is sp² here, so the unit is flat.
steps.memory_tip: sp² means flat and 120°: three OH groups spread evenly around one boron.
steps.margin_note: Label the 120° angle and write sp² beside the boron on the sketch.

steps.label: Hydrogen-bonded sheet

lines.text: Flat BO₃ units hydrogen bonded in sheets

lines: Draw three or more such units in the
same plane. The H of one OH group points
at an oxygen of the next unit; join them
with dotted lines for the hydrogen bonds.
The units link into a flat sheet, so
boric acid is a layered solid.
steps.why: The hydrogen bonds are what turn separate molecules into a layered solid, so one unit drawn on its own shows the molecule but not the structure the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Drawing the hydrogen bonds as full lines. They are weaker than the O–H bonds, so they are drawn dotted.
Drawing only one BO₃ unit. The structure is the sheet of units linked by hydrogen bonds.
Spreading the units in three directions. Each sheet is flat, and the sheets lie one above another.
steps.memory_tip: One unit is the molecule; many units joined by dotted lines are the structure.
steps.margin_note: Six units drawn in a ring show the sheet clearly, but three linked units already show the pattern. The layers slide over one another, which is why the crystals feel soapy.

insider_note: This answer is a drawing, so keep the writing down to the labels: sp², 120°, and the words hydrogen bond beside one dotted line.
